title: Remove repeat cities
prompt: Several contacts can share a city. Delete repeats so each known city keeps only its lowest id. Contacts with no city stay.
hints: Use the lowest id per city as your kept list.

check.sql: SELECT id, full_name FROM contacts ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3'); UPDATE contacts SET city = NULL WHERE id = 13; UPDATE contacts SET city = 'Murray' WHERE id = 11;

solutions: DELETE FROM contacts WHERE city IS NOT NULL AND id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM contacts WHERE city IS NOT NULL GROUP BY city);

wrongSolutions.sql: DELETE FROM contacts WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM contacts GROUP BY city);
DELETE FROM contacts WHERE city IS NOT NULL AND id NOT IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM contacts WHERE city IS NOT NULL GROUP BY city);

title: Restock
prompt: A delivery arrives: add product id 90, name Teapot, category Kitchen, price 18, cost 9, then raise all Kitchen prices by 1. Commit it as one transaction.
hints: Order matters, because the new product also gets the raise.

check.sql: SELECT id, name, category, price FROM products ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: BEGIN; INSERT INTO products (id, name, category, price, cost) VALUES (90, 'Teapot', 'Kitchen', 18, 9); UPDATE products SET price = price + 1 WHERE category = 'Kitchen'; COMMIT;

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; UPDATE products SET price = price + 1 WHERE category = 'Kitchen'; INSERT INTO products (id, name, category, price, cost) VALUES (90, 'Teapot', 'Kitchen', 18, 9); COMMIT;
wrongSolutions.why: The new product misses the raise

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; INSERT INTO products (id, name, category, price, cost) VALUES (90, 'Teapot', 'Kitchen', 18, 9); UPDATE products SET price = price + 1 WHERE category = 'Kitchen'; ROLLBACK;

title: Close a course
prompt: Course 2 is closing. Set any missing grade in it to 0, then delete all of its enrolments with a grade below 70. Use one transaction, and commit it.

check.sql: SELECT id, student_id, course_id, grade FROM enrolments ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); UPDATE enrolments SET course_id = 2 WHERE id IN (11, 13);

solutions: BEGIN; UPDATE enrolments SET grade = 0 WHERE course_id = 2 AND grade IS NULL; DELETE FROM enrolments WHERE course_id = 2 AND grade < 70; COMMIT;

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; DELETE FROM enrolments WHERE course_id = 2 AND grade < 70; UPDATE enrolments SET grade = 0 WHERE course_id = 2 AND grade IS NULL; COMMIT;
wrongSolutions.why: The missing grade survives the delete

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; UPDATE enrolments SET grade = 0 WHERE grade IS NULL; DELETE FROM enrolments WHERE grade < 70; COMMIT;

title: Reorganise a team
prompt: Department 3 is merging into department 1. In one transaction, move its employees to department 1, give each 1000 more salary, then delete department 3. Commit.
hints: Update the people before deleting the department.

check.sql: SELECT e.id, e.department_id, e.salary, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM departments) AS departments FROM employees e ORDER BY e.id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); INSERT INTO departments VALUES (3, 'Support'), (1, 'Engineering'); UPDATE employees SET department_id = 3 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET department_id = 1, salary = salary + 1000 WHERE department_id = 3; DELETE FROM departments WHERE id = 3; COMMIT;

wrongSolutions.sql: BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET department_id = 1 WHERE department_id = 3; DELETE FROM departments WHERE id = 3; COMMIT;
BEGIN; UPDATE employees SET department_id = 1, salary = salary + 1000 WHERE department_id = 3; COMMIT;
